newsitem.title: USA: Chromcraft Revington sees slowed sales.
newsitem.headline: Chromcraft Revington sees slowed sales.

text.p: Chromcraft Revington Inc sees sales orders entering the third quarter slightly behind the year-ago level, Michael Thomas, president and chief executive said.

In a statement accompanying its second quarter earnings, Thomas also said, "Second quarter shipments slowed in response to a weak retail sales environment. Excluding Cochrane Furniture, lower sales resulted primarily from a decrease in occasional furniture shipments."
Chromcraft reported net earnings for the second quarter of 1997 of $3,246,000, or $0.55 per share, compared to $3,211,000, or $.55 per share, for the year earlier quarter.
Sales for the second quarter of $54,074,000 were approximately 35 percent higher than the same period last year.
Second quarter results include the operations of Cochrane Furniture Company, Inc., which Chromcraft Revington, Inc. acquired as of November 8, 1996.
Excluding Cochrane Furniture's operating results, sales for the second quarter and first half of 1997 were slightly lower than the prior year.
Thomas said the increase in 1997 operating income from last year was offset by higher interest expense reflecting the increased debt level resulting from the Cochrane Furniture acquisition.
Chromcraft Revington designs, manufactures and sells furniture.
